sentences.text: Kamuysaurus was a herbivorous hadrosaurid dinosaur found in Late Cretaceous marine deposits near Mukawa, Hokkaido, Japan. This animal measured approximately 8 meters in length.
Its weight is estimated at 4 or 5.3 tonnes, depending on whether it was bipedal or quadrupedal.
The describing authors identified three unique derived characters, or autapomorphies, for the species.
A unique feature is a notch on the quadrate bone located at three-quarters of the shaft length from the top.
Neural spines on the sixth through thirteenth back vertebrae are inclined forward.
The holotype represents an adult individual at least nine years old.
The position of the notch on the quadrate bone is unique among all Hadrosauridae.
An amateur paleontologist discovered the tail of a euornithopod at Shirafunezawa Creek in 2003.
An entire skeleton was uncovered by museum teams in 2013 and 2014.
The species Kamuysaurus japonicus was named and described in 2019 by a team led by Professor Yoshitsugu Kobayashi.
Researchers suggest the carcass was likely washed into the sea.
Kamuysaurus belongs to the subfamily Hadrosaurinae, is classified in the family Hadrosauridae, and is a member of the class Ornithischia.
The time range for the genus is listed as the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
